questions.question: Which chamber of the human heart pumps deoxygenated blood into the pulmonary artery?

solution.key_concept: Pulmonary circulation begins at the right ventricle.
steps: In pulmonary circulation, the right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood through the pulmonary artery to the lungs.
The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta, not the pulmonary artery.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Right ventricle
solution.why_not_others: The left ventricle pumps into the aorta. The atria receive blood and do not pump into the pulmonary artery. The right atrium receives blood from the venae cavae and the left atrium receives blood from the pulmonary veins.
solution.common_trap: Assuming arteries always carry oxygenated blood. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood.
solution.time_saving_tip: Right side means deoxygenated blood going to the lungs.

questions.question: In double circulation, oxygenated blood returning from the lungs first enters which chamber of the heart, and through which vessels?
options: Right atrium, through the pulmonary veins
Left atrium, through the pulmonary veins
Left atrium, through the pulmonary artery
Left ventricle, through the venae cavae

solution.key_concept: Pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood to the left atrium.
steps: The pulmonary circuit runs from the right ventricle to the lungs and then to the left atrium.
The vessels carrying blood from the lungs to the heart are the pulmonary veins.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Left atrium, through the pulmonary veins
solution.why_not_others: The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the venae cavae. The pulmonary artery carries blood away from the heart to the lungs. The venae cavae drain the body, not the lungs.
solution.common_trap: Thinking veins always carry deoxygenated blood. The pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood.

questions.question: Stimulation of the parasympathetic nerves supplying the human heart results in:
options: Decrease in heart rate, speed of conduction and cardiac output
Increase in heart rate and strength of ventricular contraction
Decrease in heart rate but increase in cardiac output
Complete stoppage of the heartbeat, because the heart is neurogenic

solution.key_concept: The parasympathetic nervous system slows the heart.
steps: The cardiac centre in the medulla oblongata moderates heart activity through the ANS.
Parasympathetic nerves decrease heart rate, the speed of conduction and cardiac output.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Decrease in heart rate, speed of conduction and cardiac output
solution.why_not_others: Option (2) describes sympathetic stimulation. Option (3) is wrong because cardiac output also falls. Option (4) is wrong because the human heart is myogenic and only moderated by nerves.
solution.common_trap: Confusing sympathetic effects with parasympathetic effects.
solution.time_saving_tip: Parasympathetic means 'rest': everything in the heart slows down.

questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: The human heart is described as myogenic.
statements.R: The rhythmic activity of the human heart is initiated by the cardiac centre in the medulla oblongata.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Heart activity is auto-regulated by nodal tissue, and the medulla only moderates it.
steps: Heart activity is auto-regulated by nodal tissue, so the heart is myogenic. A is true.
The medullary cardiac centre only moderates this activity through the ANS and does not initiate it. R is false.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A is true but R is false
solution.why_not_others: R is false, so options (1) and (2) are wrong. A is true, so option (4) is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Treating neural moderation as if it were initiation of the heartbeat.

questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: In systemic circulation, deoxygenated blood from the tissues returns through the pulmonary veins to the left atrium.
statements.II: Sympathetic stimulation increases heart rate but decreases the strength of ventricular contraction.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: The venae cavae drain into the right atrium, and sympathetic nerves increase every measure of cardiac activity.
steps: Deoxygenated blood from the tissues returns through the veins and venae cavae to the right atrium. Statement I is incorrect.
Sympathetic nerves increase heart rate, the strength of ventricular contraction and cardiac output. Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Each statement contains a factual error, so no option that calls either statement correct can be right.
solution.common_trap: Partial-truth statements: the first half of Statement II is correct, but its second half is wrong.

questions.question: Repeated blood pressure readings at or above which value indicate hypertension?

solution.key_concept: Hypertension threshold
steps: Normal blood pressure is 120/80 mm Hg (systolic/diastolic).
Repeated readings of 140/90 mm Hg or higher indicate hypertension.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): 140/90 mm Hg
solution.why_not_others: 120/80 mm Hg is normal. 130/85 mm Hg is not the stated threshold. 90/140 mm Hg reverses systolic and diastolic values.
solution.common_trap: Reversing systolic and diastolic values.

questions.question: Heart failure is also called congestive heart failure because:
options: Heart muscle is suddenly damaged by an inadequate blood supply
Coronary arteries become congested with cholesterol deposits
Congestion of the lungs is one of its main symptoms

solution.key_concept: Heart failure and the reason for its alternative name
steps: Heart failure is the state in which the heart cannot pump blood effectively enough to meet the body's needs.
It is called congestive heart failure because congestion of the lungs is a main symptom.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Congestion of the lungs is one of its main symptoms
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) describes cardiac arrest. Option (2) describes a heart attack. Option (3) describes coronary artery disease.
solution.common_trap: Equating heart failure with cardiac arrest or a heart attack.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about angina pectoris is correct?
options: It occurs only in elderly men
It is caused mainly by congestion of the lungs
It is the condition in which the heart stops beating
It is acute chest pain that occurs when not enough oxygen reaches the heart muscle

solution.key_concept: Definition of angina pectoris
steps: Angina pectoris is acute chest pain caused by insufficient oxygen reaching the heart muscle.
It can occur at any age in men and women, though it is more common in the middle-aged and elderly.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): It is acute chest pain that occurs when not enough oxygen reaches the heart muscle
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) is wrong because angina occurs in both sexes and at any age. Lung congestion (option 2) is a feature of heart failure. Stoppage of the heartbeat (option 3) is cardiac arrest.
solution.common_trap: Reading 'more common in the elderly' as 'occurs only in the elderly'.

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: Sudden damage to heart muscle due to inadequate blood supply

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: Repeated blood pressure readings of 140/90 mm Hg or higher

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Narrowing of the lumen of vessels supplying the heart muscle by deposits

solution.key_concept: Distinguishing the circulatory disorders
steps: Hypertension is a blood pressure of 140/90 mm Hg or above (A-III).
In CAD, deposits of calcium, fat, cholesterol and fibrous tissue narrow the coronary vessels (B-IV).
In cardiac arrest the heart stops beating (C-I), while in a heart attack heart muscle is suddenly damaged (D-II).
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) swaps cardiac arrest and heart attack. Option (2) swaps hypertension and CAD. Option (3) mismatches hypertension and cardiac arrest.
solution.common_trap: Treating cardiac arrest and heart attack as the same condition.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about circulatory disorders are correct?

statements.A: Hypertension can affect vital organs such as the brain and kidney.
statements.B: Deposits of calcium, fat, cholesterol and fibrous tissue narrow the vessels in coronary artery disease.
statements.C: Heart failure and cardiac arrest are the same condition.
statements.D: Atherosclerosis mainly affects the pulmonary veins.
statements.E: Angina pectoris can occur in both men and women at any age.

options: A, B, C and E only

solution.key_concept: Facts about hypertension, CAD, angina and heart failure
steps: A is true: hypertension affects the brain and kidney.
B is true: these are the deposits found in CAD.
C is false: in heart failure the heart pumps ineffectively, while in cardiac arrest it stops beating.
D is false: atherosclerosis affects the vessels supplying the heart muscle.
E is true: angina occurs in both sexes at any age.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A, B and E only
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) omits E. Option (2) includes the false statement C. Option (3) includes the false statement D and omits A.
solution.common_trap: Accepting C because the two conditions sound similar.
solution.time_saving_tip: Rejecting C and D eliminates options (2) and (3) immediately.

questions.question: Which nitrogenous waste is excreted as a pellet or paste with minimum loss of water?

solution.key_concept: Uricotelism conserves water
steps: Toxicity and water requirement follow the order ammonia > urea > uric acid.
Uricotelic animals excrete uric acid as a pellet or paste with minimum water loss.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Uric acid
solution.why_not_others: Urea needs more water than uric acid. Ammonia, excreted as $NH_4^+$, needs the most water.
solution.common_trap: Thinking urea is the least water-demanding waste.

questions.question: Which of the following groups consists only of ureotelic animals?
options: Mammals, terrestrial amphibians and marine fishes
Bony fishes, aquatic amphibians and aquatic insects

solution.key_concept: Classifying animals by their mode of excretion
steps: Ureotelic animals include mammals, many terrestrial amphibians and marine fishes.
Birds are uricotelic, and bony fishes are ammonotelic.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Mammals, terrestrial amphibians and marine fishes
solution.why_not_others: Option (2) lists ammonotelic animals. Option (3) lists uricotelic animals. Option (4) includes birds, which are uricotelic.
solution.common_trap: Grouping marine fishes with ammonotelic bony fishes.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of an animal and its excretory structure is correct?

solution.key_concept: Excretory structures in different animals
steps: Prawns and other crustaceans have antennal (green) glands.
Earthworms have nephridia, insects such as the cockroach have Malpighian tubules, and flatworms have protonephridia.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Prawn – green glands
solution.why_not_others: Options (2) and (3) swap the excretory structures of the earthworm and the cockroach. Flatworms have flame cells, not antennal glands.
solution.common_trap: Swapping nephridia and Malpighian tubules between the earthworm and the cockroach.

questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: In ammonotelic animals, the kidneys play no significant role in the elimination of ammonia.
statements.R: Ammonia is the least toxic nitrogenous waste and requires very little water for its elimination.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Ammonotelism
steps: Ammonotelic animals excrete $NH_4^+$ by diffusion across body surfaces or gills, and the kidneys play no significant role. A is true.
Ammonia is the most toxic waste and needs the most water. R is false.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A is true but R is false
solution.why_not_others: R is false, so options (1), (2) and (4) are all wrong.
solution.common_trap: Reversing the toxicity order of the nitrogenous wastes.

questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Protonephridia (flame cells) of flatworms function mainly in the elimination of nitrogenous wastes rather than in osmoregulation.
statements.II: Marine fishes are ammonotelic, while terrestrial amphibians are uricotelic.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: The function of protonephridia and the ureotelic groups
steps: Protonephridia function mainly in osmoregulation. Statement I is incorrect.
Marine fishes and terrestrial amphibians are both ureotelic. Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are false, so every other option fails.
solution.common_trap: Assuming every excretory structure works mainly in nitrogen removal.

questions.question: The human kidneys are located between which vertebrae?
options: Last thoracic and third lumbar vertebrae
First thoracic and third thoracic vertebrae
Third lumbar and first sacral vertebrae
Last cervical and first thoracic vertebrae

solution.key_concept: Position of the kidneys
steps: The kidneys are bean-shaped.
They lie between the last thoracic and third lumbar vertebrae.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Last thoracic and third lumbar vertebrae
solution.why_not_others: Options (2) and (4) place the kidneys too high. Option (3) places them too low.
solution.common_trap: Placing the kidneys entirely within the lumbar region.

questions.question: The normal glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of a healthy human is approximately:

solution.key_concept: Glomerular filtration rate
steps: GFR is about 125 mL/min.
Converting to a daily figure: 125 mL × 1440 min = 180,000 mL, or about 180 L per day.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): 125 mL per minute
solution.why_not_others: Option (2) applies the daily number 180 to a per-minute unit. Option (3) is the daily urine output. Option (4) applies the per-minute number 125 to a per-day unit.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the GFR units with the urine output figures.

questions.question: Which part of the nephron is impermeable to water but transports electrolytes?

solution.key_concept: Permeability of the two limbs of Henle's loop
steps: The descending limb is permeable to water.
The ascending limb is impermeable to water but transports electrolytes.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Ascending limb of Henle's loop
solution.why_not_others: The descending limb is permeable to water. The PCT reabsorbs 70 to 80% of the water. The collecting duct reabsorbs much water to concentrate urine.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the two limbs of Henle's loop.

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: I
list_II.text: Extensions of the cortex between the medullary pyramids

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: Notch through which the ureter, blood vessels and nerves enter or leave

solution.key_concept: Structures of the kidney and the nephron
steps: The hilum is the notch for the ureter, blood vessels and nerves (A-II).
The columns of Bertini are cortical extensions between the pyramids (B-I).
The Malpighian body is the glomerulus plus Bowman's capsule (C-IV), and the PCT has cuboidal brush-border epithelium (D-III).
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) swaps the hilum and the columns of Bertini. Option (2) swaps the Malpighian body and the PCT. Option (4) swaps the hilum and the Malpighian body.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the columns of Bertini with the medullary pyramids.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about urine formation are correct?

statements.A: The medullary osmolarity gradient ranges from 300 to 1200 mOsmol per L and is maintained by NaCl and urea.
statements.B: Urine can become nearly ten times as concentrated as the initial filtrate.
statements.C: The PCT secretes $H^+$, $NH_3$ and $K^+$, helping to maintain pH.
statements.D: Cortical nephrons have long loops of Henle that dip deep into the medulla.
statements.E: Daily urine output is 1 to 1.5 L, containing 25 to 30 g of urea.

options: A, C, D and E only

solution.key_concept: Concentration of urine and functions of the nephron
steps: A is true.
B is false: urine becomes nearly four times as concentrated as the filtrate.
C is true.
D is false: cortical nephrons have short loops, while juxtamedullary nephrons have long ones.
E is true.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A, C and E only
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) includes the false statement B. Option (2) includes the false statement D and omits A. Option (3) includes the false statement D.
solution.common_trap: Attributing the long loops of juxtamedullary nephrons to cortical nephrons.
solution.time_saving_tip: Rejecting B and D leaves only option (4).
